title: DOJ begins forfeiture proceedings for more than $1 billion in USDC tied to Binance theft
date_note: Fox Business, published 23 November, says the Justice Department said Monday; Cointelegraph (23 November) says the filing was Monday. Neither gives an earlier day.
geo_basis: the federal court in Washington, DC, as Cointelegraph states
summary: Fox Business reports the Justice Department said Monday it has begun legal proceedings to recover more than $1 billion in USDC held across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains, tied to the October 29 Binance hack. Cointelegraph reports prosecutors asked a federal court in Washington, DC, to permanently forfeit more than $1.1 billion. Fox Business says North Korean hackers are blamed; Cointelegraph says US authorities link the attack to TraderTraitor.
plain: The US Justice Department has started court proceedings to recover crypto stolen in the October 29 Binance hack. Fox Business reports more than $1 billion; Cointelegraph reports more than $1.1 billion.
exec: US prosecutors are seeking to forfeit USDC from the Binance theft; the two outlets give more than $1 billion (Fox Business) and more than $1.1 billion (Cointelegraph).

evidence.quote: The U.S. government has begun legal proceedings to recover more than $1 billion in cryptocurrency
held across 36 virtual currency addresses spanning 18 different blockchain networks
The US Department of Justice is seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in crypto
prosecutors asked a federal court in Washington, DC, to permanently forfeit the funds

validation.note: Fox Business and Cointelegraph each report the DOJ action; they differ on the amount (more than $1 billion vs more than $1.1 billion). The DOJ's own release was not found or read.

review.note: Compared amounts, 36 addresses/18 chains, Monday 23 Nov, TraderTraitor against Fox Business and Cointelegraph
